    Learner Profiles

    OnDemand Portal Orientation - Learner Profiles

    Alex Chen (Graduate Student)

    Background

    • PhD student in molecular biology
    • Strong experimentalist but limited computational experience
    • Has SSH access but hasn’t mastered it
    • Uses Windows laptop at home
    • Works with large microscopy image datasets (100+ GB)

    Motivation for OnDemand

    • Wants to process data without SSH overhead
    • Needs to share analysis with lab group
    • Prefers visual interfaces

    What Alex Gets from This Workshop

    • Comfort with graphical file management
    • Realizes can upload/download large files reliably
    • Learns how to run Jupyter for image analysis
    • Understands how to request help in clear way

    Alex’s Success Metrics

    • Successfully uploads large dataset
    • Runs Jupyter notebook for image processing
    • Submits a batch job for overnight analysis
    • Knows where to find help

    Jamal Thompson (Undergrad Research)

    Background

    • Sophomore majoring in physics and computer science
    • First HPC experience
    • Has Python experience from CS classes
    • MacBook user, comfortable with terminal concepts
    • Working on summer research project

    Motivation for OnDemand

    • Wants to run simulations on supercomputer
    • Excited about GPU computing
    • Prefers graphical tools initially but open to SSH later

    What Jamal Gets from This Workshop

    • Realizes OnDemand is good entry point, can graduate to SSH later
    • Learns GPU job submission
    • Gets comfortable with job submission and monitoring
    • Understands resource requests

    Jamal’s Success Metrics

    • Submits successful GPU job
    • Views output and understands results
    • Moves to SSH-based workflow in future training
    • Attends GPU Computing workshop next

    Dr. Priya Patel (Faculty)

    Background

    • Assistant professor in neuroscience
    • Leads group of 5 undergrads and graduate students
    • Limited time for computing administration
    • Works across Mac and Windows
    • Needs to monitor student work

    Motivation for OnDemand

    • Monitor what students are doing on cluster
    • Make sure storage isn’t overused
    • Provide basic training without effort
    • Manage group’s resource allocation

    What Priya Gets from This Workshop

    • Understands how her students experience HPC
    • Can monitor disk usage and jobs via web interface
    • Knows how to demonstrate features to students
    • Realizes when to escalate to HPC staff

    Priya’s Success Metrics

    • Can check her group’s disk quota
    • Understands job statuses her students report
    • Can guide students to help resources
    • Feels confident in cluster use

    Marcus Williams (Career Changer)

    Background

    • Career changer into data science
    • Bootcamp graduate, learning HPC for first time
    • Uses Linux laptop, comfortable with basics
    • First serious research computing experience
    • Working on capstone project

    Motivation for OnDemand

    • Avoid overwhelm of full command line initially
    • Focus on learning data science concepts
    • Build confidence gradually

    What Marcus Gets from This Workshop

    • Validates his Linux knowledge works here
    • Realizes HPC isn’t as scary as expected
    • Excited to submit first job successfully
    • Plans to learn command line next

    Marcus’s Success Metrics

    • Submits and monitors first HPC job successfully
    • Practices on small example before big data
    • Attends next workshop on command-line training

    Diana Garcia (Visiting Scholar)

    Background

    • Visiting postdoc from another country
    • Working here for 1 year on collaborative research
    • Limited English; tech-savvy but learning platform is new
    • Uses tablet and small laptop
    • Wants self-sufficient computing

    Motivation for OnDemand

    • Graphical interface easier to use with language barrier
    • Visual cues help understanding

    What Diana Gets from This Workshop

    • Comfort with visual navigation despite language challenges
    • Realizes can accomplish work with OnDemand alone
    • Gets contact for support in multiple formats

    Common Learner Patterns

    Pattern 1: “I just want to run my code”

    These learners want quick results with minimum complexity. They appreciate that OnDemand gets them computing faster without SSH mastery.

    Pattern 2: “I like to understand systems”

    These learners want to know why things work this way. Connecting OnDemand features to underlying SLURM helps them learn better.

    Pattern 3: “I prefer graphical interfaces”

    These learners gravitate toward OnDemand immediately and may never feel comfortable with SSH. Help them succeed with graphical tools.

    Pattern 4: “I want to be a power user”

    These learners see OnDemand as stepping stone to SSH and advanced HPC. Encourage them toward next workshops.

    Differentiated Support

    For Complete Beginners

    • Extra emphasis on dashboard navigation
    • Pre-recorded tutorials for review
    • Hands-on help with first file upload
    • Celebrate small wins

    For Experienced Linux Users

    • Skip basic terminal coverage
    • Focus on OnDemand-specific features
    • Faster pace through file management
    • Early GPU computing introduction

    For ESL Learners

    • Clear written instructions in addition to verbal
    • Visual demonstrations with minimal speech
    • Extra breaks for processing time
    • Contact info in multiple formats

    Tips for Instructors

    • Recognize that not everyone arrives at HPC with same background
    • Learner profiles help anticipate questions and needs
    • Create multiple examples for different research areas
    • Have both fast and slow paths through material
    • Celebrate diverse backgrounds learners bring
